reconcile.note: Gill reads Jesus's ban on anxious worry about tomorrow as compatible with the ordinary, lawful diligence Paul later requires for providing one's household.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Gerd Theissen catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Gerd Theissen, The First Followers of Jesus: A Sociological Analysis of the Earliest Christianity (1978).

sides.snippet: Therefore don't be anxious, saying, 'What will we eat?', 'What will we drink?' or, 'With what will we be clothed?'
sides.verseText: \"Therefore don't be anxious, saying, 'What will we eat?', 'What will we drink?' or, 'With what will we be clothed?'

sides.snippet: But if anyone doesn't provide for his own, and especially his own household, he has denied the faith, and is worse than an unbeliever.
sides.verseText: But if anyone doesn't provide for his own, and especially his own household, he has denied the faith, and is worse than an unbeliever.
